answers.plain:
**Subject:** Following up from the Midwest Hospitality Expo

Hi [First Name],

Thanks for stopping by our booth at the Midwest Hospitality Expo last week. I enjoyed our conversation about [specific detail, e.g., keeping shrink under control / tracking inventory across multiple suppliers] at your store.

As I mentioned, we build inventory software designed for independent grocers. One of our customers, a store in Dayton, saw real results after switching. You can read the case study here: [link]

I'd be happy to show you how it would work for [Store Name] in a quick 15-minute demo. Do you have time this week or next? Just reply with a day and time that suits you, or grab a slot here: [scheduling link, optional].

Thanks again, and I look forward to talking soon.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Title] | [Company]
[Phone] | [Email]

---

**Tips:**
- Since you met about 30 people, the booth-conversation line is what makes this feel personal. Even a few words of specifics per person will help a lot.
- If you have a headline number from the Dayton case study (e.g., "cut spoilage by X%"), add it to the second paragraph. It's more compelling than a generic reference to results.
- Send only to the people who asked about the grocery software, as you planned. Others might need a different note.

I can also write a shorter version, or a second email for follow-ups if they don't reply.
answers.nudge:
# Follow-up email

**Subject line options** (pick one, A/B test if your tool allows):
- Following up from the Expo, {{first_name}}
- {{Store name}} + inventory: 15 minutes?
- How a Dayton grocer cut {{result}}: the case study I mentioned

**Body:**

> Hi {{first_name}},
>
> Good meeting you at the Midwest Hospitality Expo last week. I enjoyed our conversation about {{specific detail: e.g., shrink on produce / ordering across two locations / their current spreadsheet setup}}.
>
> You asked about how our inventory software works for independent grocers. The closest example is {{Dayton store name}} in Dayton, who {{one concrete result: e.g., cut spoilage by X% and saved Y hours a week on ordering}}. Here's the short case study: {{link}}
>
> I'd be glad to show you what it would look like for {{their store}}. Do you have 15 minutes this week or next? You can grab a time here: {{calendar link}}. If it's easier, reply with a day that works and I'll send an invite.
>
> Thanks again for stopping by,
> {{Your name}}
> {{Title, company}} | {{phone}}

## Why it's built this way
- **The personal line carries the email.** Prospects who got a generic message after a trade show often ignore it, and one real detail from the booth conversation changes that. Spend 60 seconds per person on it.
- **The case study comes with one number.** A bare link gets skipped, but a stated result gives them a reason to click.
- **There are two ways to say yes.** They can book on the calendar link or reply with a day. Both are low-effort.
- **There's one ask.** It's a 15-minute demo, with no deck or "pick my brain" request.

## Before you send
1. **Segment the 30 people.** Send this version only to those who asked about the grocery software. Others get a lighter "nice to meet you" note.
2. **Fill in the Dayton result with a number you can back up.** Get the store's sign-off if the case study doesn't already name them and the figures.
3. **Send Tuesday through Thursday, mid-morning, in the recipient's time zone.** You're already a week out, so send soon. Today is Monday, Oct 26, so sending tomorrow works well.
4. **Send individually from your own address**, not as a bulk blast. This helps deliverability and replies.

## Follow-up sequence if they don't reply
- **Day 4 (short bump):** "Hi {{first_name}}, floating this back up in case it got buried. Happy to do a quick 15 minutes, or I can send a 2-minute walkthrough video if you'd prefer."
- **Day 10 (give value):** Send one useful item, such as a short checklist on reducing grocery shrink or a relevant stat. Close with: "If the timing isn't right, no worries. Should I check back in January?"
- **Then stop.** After three touches, move them to a nurture list.

If you paste in the Dayton results and a few of your booth notes, I can fill in the placeholders and draft personalized openers for each person.

**Subject:** Counting stock at your store: a Dayton grocer's story

Hi [First name],

It was good talking with you at the Midwest Hospitality Expo. You mentioned [what they said at the booth], and that stuck with me, because it's the same problem we hear from a lot of independent grocers.

One of our customers, a store in Dayton, was in a similar spot. The result their owner talks about most: "I stopped finding out something was out of stock when a customer told me." Here's the full story: [case study link]

I'd like to show you how it would work for your store. Could we do a 15-minute demo this week or next? You can pick a time here: [scheduling link]

Warmly,
[my name]

---

**Note:** I don't have the Dayton case study, so I wrote that quote as a placeholder. Before sending, swap in the result the study actually reports (for example, less spoilage, fewer stockouts, or hours saved on counts), phrased the way an owner would say it. Don't send a quote or figure the study doesn't support.
